title: pm-dispatch SKILL structural compression: 3050 → ~1400–1600 lines (PR₂ of batch #7631, maintainer-directed)
body:
Handoff card filed by the skills seat (#7623, session `session_01ATJiqhFNL82YwV8udPkoqX`) — the session ran out of budget mid-batch and the maintainer directed the remainder be filed for another seat to pick up. This is **PR₂ of batch #7631**; PR₁ (the eight ruled amendments) merged at 2026-08-11 11:45Z as PR #7698, so this card is unblocked and dispatchable now.

## Maintainer directive (verbatim, untranslated — skills seat 专题讨论, 2026-08-11)

> 现在 的 项目经理skills 太长了,需要考虑怎么压缩

Delivery shape (PR₁ then PR₂, pure moves last) was accepted in the same exchange and is recorded on #7631.

## Measured starting state (`origin/main` after PR #7698 — re-measure at work time, do not trust these)

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` = **3050 lines**, sitting exactly on the `check:pm-skill-ratchet` ceiling (3050, config at `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`). `references/incidents.md` = 437 lines (append-only). `references/compile-surfaces.md` = 27.

Composition measured before PR₁ (shape still holds; re-derive the numbers):

| section | lines |
|---|---|
| The round loop | 1870 — step 5 Dispatch 587 (Prompt template 326), step 7 Review 380, step 0 sweep 200, step 6 Collect 195, 入队与落地 167, step 8 130 |
| Operational notes | 612 (21 notes, each = rule + incident narrative) |
| Domain lanes | 209 (incl. the `spec-tooling` 沿革 111, self-labelled "沿革, 不是待办") |
| State model / Epic / Guardrails / report contract | ~300, mostly load-bearing |

## Target and method

- **Target ~1400–1600 lines** in the main file (roughly −50%).
- **Every rule keeps three things in the main file**: the imperative, its criteria/command, and a one-line case anchor (issue number). Narratives, 沿革, worked examples and incident retellings move **verbatim** to `references/incidents.md` (append-only, one 出处 line per section, matching the convention PR #7698 established with 24 such moves) or a new `references/operational-notes.md` if the notes section warrants its own file.
- **Machine-consumed content stays**: domain-lane table, 词表 roster, seat/label setup loop, the escalation frame (all four gate-synchronized copies — `check:skill-frame-sync`), report contract JSON.
- ⛔ **No rule deletion.** Compression moves prose; removing a binding rule, criterion, or prohibition requires its own maintainer ruling. A reviewer must be able to diff old→new and see every imperative still present.
- **Ratchet**: lower the ceiling to the achieved count (shrink-only lock-in) in the same PR.

## Constraints

- File surface: `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/**`, the ratchet config. ⛔ No `docs/adr/**`, no `content/docs/releases/**`.
- **ADR-class terminal state** (#7548, now live in SKILL.md step 7 + Guardrails): draft/review by AI seats; ⛔ no AI seat merges, enqueues, or arms auto-merge — the maintainer merges manually. Round reports carry an "awaiting a human merge" line until it lands.
- Dispatch tier: **`model: claude-fable-5` mandatory** (any card editing `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`, maintainer 2026-08-10), `mode:cloud`. ⚠️ The filing session exhausted its Fable budget — whoever picks this up needs headroom for an L-sized card.
- `skip-changeset` label (`.claude/` only; #5471 rejects empty changesets).
- Gates for this surface: `check:pm-skill-ratchet`, `check:skill-frame-sync`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:nul-bytes`, plus `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` after building the lint dependency closure.
- Sanitizer discipline on every SKILL.md write (HTML entities for literal angle brackets; read back and verify fragments survived).
- `Fixes` this card + `Part of #7631`; close #7631 when this lands.

## Prior art to reuse

PR #7698's diff is the pattern: each moved section left an anchor + pointer in place and gained an 出处 line at the destination. The cloud dev session that did PR₁ (`session_01KCFsFypEHm1Cnp26yAofxg`, now archived) sketched this plan in its report's `open_questions[2]` on #7631.
